source: NCERT Class VIII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Shivaji and the Maratha State
points: **Shivaji (1630–1680)** founded the Maratha kingdom in the western Deccan, resisting the **Mughals (Aurangzeb)** and the **Bijapur** sultanate.
He was crowned **Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674**.
Famous for **guerrilla warfare (ganimi kava)** and a network of **hill forts**.
His daring escape from **Aurangzeb's** court at Agra (1666) is legendary.

sections.heading: 2. Shivaji's Administration
points: A council of **eight ministers = the Ashtapradhan**; chief minister = **Peshwa**.
Efficient **revenue system**; levied **chauth** (¼ of revenue) and **sardeshmukhi** (⅒) on neighbouring territories.
Promoted **Marathi and Sanskrit**; a strong **navy** to guard the Konkan coast.
Known for **religious tolerance** and care for peasants.

sections.heading: 3. The Peshwas and Maratha Expansion
points: After Shivaji, real power passed to the **Peshwas** (hereditary chief ministers) based at **Poona (Pune)** — e.g. **Baji Rao I**.
The Marathas expanded across much of India as a **confederacy** of chiefs — **Scindias (Gwalior), Holkars (Indore), Gaekwads (Baroda), Bhonsles (Nagpur)**.
Their advance was checked at the **Third Battle of Panipat (1761)** by Ahmad Shah Abdali — a huge setback.
The Marathas revived but were finally defeated by the **British** in the **Anglo-Maratha Wars**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad, 1674; used guerrilla warfare (ganimi kava) & hill forts.
Ashtapradhan = council of 8 ministers; chief minister = Peshwa.
Maratha levies: chauth (¼) and sardeshmukhi (⅒).
Peshwas (Poona) led expansion; confederacy: Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad, Bhonsle.
Third Battle of Panipat 1761 = Maratha defeat by Abdali.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Shivaji was crowned **Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674**.
**Chauth = ¼**, **sardeshmukhi = ⅒** of revenue.
The **Ashtapradhan** was Shivaji's council of **eight** ministers.
The Maratha **confederacy** houses: **Scindia (Gwalior), Holkar (Indore), Gaekwad (Baroda), Bhonsle (Nagpur)**.
